title: LEGOSim: A Unified Parallel Simulation Framework for Multi-chiplet Heterogeneous Integration
problem: Simulating heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems (e.g., CPU+GPU+CIM chiplets integrated on an interposer) is not supported by existing simulators (gem5, GPGPU-Sim) because they lack modular composition of heterogeneous chiplet models and suffer from prohibitive synchronization overhead in parallel simulation—per-cycle global synchronization can waste up to 99.9% of simulation time on barrier overhead.
motivation: The industry shift to chiplet-based heterogeneous integration (SIMBA, CXL memory, CIM accelerators) requires accurate performance simulation tools, but no unified framework allows plugging diverse chiplet simulators together with acceptable speed and accuracy.
method: LEGOSim wraps each chiplet simulator as an independent parallel process (simlet) that runs on its own schedule rather than waiting at every cycle. Synchronization is on-demand: each simlet advances through adaptable time windows (time quanta) and only stops to exchange messages when one chiplet actually needs to communicate with another, eliminating expensive global synchronization barriers. A separate simulator handles the network connecting the chiplets, tracking message latency, bandwidth, and routing. Testing on SIMBA (a multi-chiplet neural network accelerator) and a CiM-based accelerator showed simulation errors of 3.79% and 3.94% respectively.
key_novelty: The core idea is using on-demand synchronization with adaptive time windows: chiplet simulators advance independently and only pause to exchange messages when cross-chiplet communication actually occurs, eliminating the global synchronization barriers that were consuming up to 99.9% of simulation time.
contributions: LEGOSim parallel simulation framework that integrates heterogeneous chiplet simulators as independent parallel processes (simlets) with minimal code modification
On-demand synchronization protocol with adaptive time quanta and non-global fencing, eliminating unnecessary barriers while preserving correctness
Integrated Network-on-Interposer (NoI) simulator for accurate modeling of inter-chiplet communication and interconnect topology
Validation against SIMBA and CiM accelerator architectures with <4% average error; synchronization overhead reduced by 99.9% vs. per-cycle sync and 66.1% vs. fixed-quantum sync

metrics.accuracy: 3.79% and 3.94% average simulation error vs. real hardware (SIMBA and CiM accelerator)
metrics.other: Synchronization overhead reduced by up to 99.9% vs. per-cycle sync; 66.1% reduction vs. fixed-quantum sync

limitations: Validation is limited to two specific multi-chiplet systems; scalability to large numbers of heterogeneous simlets with complex cross-chiplet dependency patterns is not analyzed.
primary_theme: parallel simulation framework for heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems
